title: Add feature flags + emergency kill switch for Dedicated Burst capacity
author: Benji Okafor
description: Context: Dedicated Burst capacity is rolling out behind guardrails and we need deterministic gating + a fast rollback path that does not depend on code deploys. This PR introduces feature flags and a global kill switch for burst admission, plus safe defaults for all existing/new tenants. Summary of changes: (1) Feature flags: adds a policy-evaluated boolean `burst_enabled` gate that must be true before routing/gateway can request burst capacity, and a separate `burst_admission_enabled` gate on the admission controller side (defense-in-depth). (2) Emergency kill switch: adds `burst_global_kill_switch` which, when flipped, forces all burst admission decisions to DENY with a consistent denial reason code and a short TTL cache to avoid thundering herds during an incident. (3) Region/hardware allowlist: adds a rollout allowlist (`burst_allowed_regions`, `burst_allowed_hw_classes`) to constrain burst to specific fleet pools while we ramp capacity. (4) Safe defaults: for all tenants (including new tenants) burst is disabled unless explicitly enabled via tenant config; for new regions/hw the default is deny until added to allowlist. (5) Observability hooks: emits a metric + structured log for kill-switch denies and includes a flag snapshot in admission decision traces (redacted). Behavior/semantics: a request is eligible for burst only if (a) tenant has burst enabled in tenant config AND (b) region/hw is allowlisted AND (c) global kill switch is off AND (d) admission controller feature flag is enabled. If any gate fails, we return an immediate deny (no queuing) with reason codes: `BURST_DISABLED_TENANT`, `BURST_DISABLED_REGION`, `BURST_DISABLED_HW_CLASS`, or `BURST_DISABLED_GLOBAL`. Notes: reason codes align with pr-23795 so Support/CS can explain denials; kill switch deny is intentionally fast and does not consult telemetry/fairness to keep incident behavior predictable. Testing: unit tests for policy evaluation + precedence, integration tests for routing path honoring deny reasons, and a manual runbook step validated in staging (flip kill switch and verify denial propagation within <60s). Rollout plan: ship behind internal-only flag, enable in staging, then dogfood `us-east/H100` allowlist before beta tenants. Follow-ups: (a) wire kill switch flips into oncall tooling + incident templates, (b) add alert annotations linking to runbook, (c) docs for customers on expected 429/retry behavior when burst is denied.

review_conversation: Jordan Lee: Can we confirm precedence? I want global kill switch to override everything, regardless of tenant config. Also please ensure determinism under telemetry lag (no telemetry reads when kill switch is on).
Benji Okafor (author): Yep — kill switch short-circuits before telemetry/fairness. Added tests for precedence order and ensured the handler returns before fetching telemetry snapshots.
Sean Gallagher: From an oncall standpoint, need a single switch we can flip during an incident and a metric that clearly indicates kill switch is active + the volume of denied burst attempts.
Benji Okafor (author): Added `burst_kill_switch_active{region,hw}` gauge and `burst_denied_total{reason}` counter. Also added structured log field `gating_reason` so incident searches are easy.
Mina Haddad: Routing needs to treat BURST_DISABLED_* as a hard deny and avoid retry loops. Do we have guidance on TTL/backoff so clients don’t hammer admission?
Benji Okafor (author): Routing path now treats these as terminal denials (no internal retry). The deny response includes a `retry_after_ms` hint (set to 1000ms on kill switch denies, 0 otherwise).
Keiko Yamamoto: Default allowlist should be empty for new regions/hw until Fleet provisions a pool. Please don’t accidentally enable burst on new SKUs via shared defaults.
Benji Okafor (author): Confirmed defaults: empty allowlist; deny by default. Added a comment + a regression test in defaults.yaml.
Ethan Park: Please add validation that tenant-level burst enablement cannot be set if global allowlist does not include the tenant’s region/hw (we can warn but should not hard fail).
Benji Okafor (author): Implemented a non-blocking validation warning (audit log + console warning) but allows config to be set ahead of capacity provisioning.
notable_ci_events: 2025-03-29: integration tests failed once due to flaky staging dependency; re-run passed after isolating test to hermetic fake policy engine
2025-03-31: final CI green after addressing reviewer feedback on precedence + metrics labels
release_notes: Dedicated: Burst capacity can now be gated per-tenant and per-region/hardware via feature flags.
SRE: Added a global burst kill switch for fast rollback and safer incident response.
Observability: New metrics/log fields to distinguish burst denies due to gating vs capacity/fairness.
